run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The frontend's user-facing GET /recommendations path is failing with HTTP 500, and the evidence points to a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy as the applied fault: NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation in namespace hotel-reservation declares policyTypes [Ingress, Egress] with no ingress or egress rules and selects pod label io.kompose.service=recommendation, which is carried by pod recommendation-86cf75495d-fdghh. The policy was created at 2026-11-23T22:20:36Z; the recommendation container had already started and registered itself in Consul at 22:20:32Z and its pod is Running, ready, with 0 restarts, yet from 22:20:47.79Z frontend traces show HTTP GET /recommendations returning 500 with a child client span /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations failing in ~26 microseconds (an immediate local gRPC failure with no network round trip) and no recommendation server span. recommendation is also absent from the 7 services Jaeger has recorded. In the same sample, frontend HTTP GET /hotels returned 200 with successful child calls to search, profile and reservation, so the failure is specific to the recommendation dependency. Rate/search throttling counters were all zero and the mongo admin-privilege fault scripts in ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate show no sign of having been applied, so neither is supported as the cause. Observed impact is the frontend /recommendations endpoint; the evidence does not show any other caller of recommendation.

claims.text: Frontend spans show HTTP GET /recommendations failing: trace 1210d3ce7e5a0d91 contains only two spans, both from service frontend - the root HTTP GET /recommendations span with status tags error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR (duration 84us) and its child client span /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR (duration 26us) - and no recommendation server span.

In the 20 sampled frontend traces returned for 2026-11-23T21:20:48Z-22:20:48Z (all spans starting 22:20:47.799Z-22:20:47.982Z), 10 were HTTP GET /recommendations spans with http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR whose child client spans /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations lasted 15-26us, while 10 were HTTP GET /hotels spans with http.status_code=200 whose children /search.Search/Nearby, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability carried no error tags.

NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation in namespace hotel-reservation has spec.podSelector matchLabels {io.kompose.service: recommendation}, spec.policyTypes [Ingress, Egress], and both spec.ingress and spec.egress are null, i.e. no traffic is allowed in either direction.

NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation was created at 2026-11-23T22:20:36Z and its only managedFields writer is manager OpenAPI-Generator (Update at 2026-11-23T22:20:36Z); it is the only NetworkPolicy present in the cluster at query time.

Pod recommendation-86cf75495d-fdghh carries labels io.kompose.service=recommendation and pod-template-hash=86cf75495d, is in phase Running, and its container hotel-reserv-recommendation is ready with restart count 0 - so it matches the deny-all policy's selector.

The recommendation container logged normal startup through 2026-11-23T22:20:32Z including 'Read database URL: mongodb-recommendation:27017', 'New session successfull...', 'Generating test data...', 'Trying to register service [ name: srv-recommendation, id: b1fd5fb5-d085-4205-bcda-0ecf6b7791f9, address: 10.244.125.27:8085 ]' and 'Successfully registered in consul'; no error line was logged, and its last line (22:20:32.249Z) predates the policy creation at 22:20:36Z.
Jaeger's service list contains exactly 7 services - frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search, user - and recommendation is not among them.

All 19 hotel-reservation pods were Running with ready containers and restart count 0 at query time, and Deployment status showed readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1 for consul, frontend, geo, jaeger, memcached-profile, memcached-rate, memcached-reserve, mongodb-geo, mongodb-profile, mongodb-rate, mongodb-recommendation, mongodb-reservation, mongodb-user, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search and user.

Kubernetes events in the window (source range 2026-11-23T21:22:46Z-22:20:38Z) show no Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff pod event; the only hotel-reservation Pod failures are two FailedScheduling messages saying the pod no longer existed during VolumeBinding ('pod "mongodb-geo-78487c9767-kc72g" not found', 'pod "mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-qnp7t" not found'), both at 22:20:26Z, and the only Unhealthy event is a 503 readiness-probe miss on loki-0 in namespace observe.

The application was freshly rolled out inside the window: hotel-reservation Deployment events show replica sets scaling 0 to 1 between 22:20:23Z and 22:20:27Z, and the frontend Deployment produced a second ReplicaSet frontend-8688fc47d8 at 22:20:37Z while ReplicaSet frontend-68745cb99c (created 22:20:23Z, replicas 0) has an identical container image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation@sha256:1c685e1c4c304f327952397b3a99c54dadb086607774d71f222b200ec0d2e65e and identical env (JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1) and args.

The rate/throttling path shows no rejection: at 2026-11-23T22:20:48Z rate_requests_rejected_total=0, rate_requests_expired_total=0, rate_queue_depth=0, rate_in_flight=0, rate_backend_qps_limit=500, rate_queue_capacity=256, rate_requests_received_total=5 and rate_requests_completed_total=5; on the search side search_rate_attempts_total=0, search_rate_failures_total=0, search_rate_timeouts_total=0, search_rate_successes_total=0 and search_requests_total=0.

The mongo administrative-privilege fault scenarios exist only as dormant scripts in ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate (revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh and revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh revoke the admin user's readWrite role), and no observed log shows them applied: rate logged 'New session successfull...', 'Generating test data...' and 'Successfull', geo logged a successful DB session and test-data generation, and mongodb-rate logged 'Authentication succeeded' for principalName admin on authenticationDatabase admin.

Service discovery and registration for the dependency exist rather than being missing: service recommendation is a ClusterIP on port 8085 with selector io.kompose.service=recommendation, and the recommendation process registered srv-recommendation to Consul at 10.244.125.27:8085, so the 500s are not explained by a missing Service object or unregistered instance.

Root cause hypothesis: NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation (namespace hotel-reservation, Ingress+Egress selected on io.kompose.service=recommendation with empty rule lists, created 2026-11-23T22:20:36Z) blocks the frontend's gRPC calls to recommendation-86cf75495d-fdghh on 8085 and blocks the recommendation container's own traffic, which would explain the ~26us frontend client-span failures, the HTTP 500 on GET /recommendations, the absent recommendation server spans in trace 1210d3ce7e5a0d91, and recommendation's absence from Jaeger's service list.

Rejected: that a crashed, unschedulable or resource-starved workload caused the failures. Every hotel-reservation pod was Running and ready with 0 restarts, every Deployment reported readyReplicas equal to availableReplicas, and no Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff pod event was recorded in the window, so a broken workload is not supported as the cause of the /recommendations 500s.

Recommendation (not executed): add explicit rules to deny-all-recommendation - ingress from the frontend pods to recommendation on TCP 8085, and egress from recommendation to mongodb-recommendation:27017 and to otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local:6831 - or remove the deny-all policy if the segmentation was not intended, then re-verify that frontend HTTP GET /recommendations returns 200 and that recommendation server spans appear in Jaeger.

gaps: No pre-incident baseline exists: all pods were created 22:20:23-22:20:27Z, the traces returned span only 22:20:47.799Z-22:20:47.982Z, and the rate_/search_ metric series hold a single sample at 2026-11-23T22:20:48Z, so I cannot show whether GET /recommendations returned 200 earlier, when the 500s actually began, or any latency trend.

A traces query for service recommendation over 22:20:36Z-22:20:48Z returned no data (view 87b821a1-c7c9-4eb9-8ad2-b5a6acf6f3c0-t1:b8ee0c49-a665-421a-90b3-d909ae54de89, status no_data), so the absence of recommendation server spans rests on the sampled frontend traces and Jaeger's service list, not a complete trace store; recommendation's own request-level errors remain unobserved.

Views that returned no data leave these signals unchecked rather than zero: the Prometheus span-metric queries over {__name__=~"traces_.*"} and traces_span_metrics_calls_total (2b257b8e-8d3d-4f34-b15e-9328eb3b504b-t0:51cdb574-e25a-43ef-9910-59e779316bd3 and 2b257b8e-8d3d-4f34-b15e-9328eb3b504b-t1:72cb52ab-7595-4ffe-8cf4-d8f6ee496e83) returned nothing, as did kube_pod_container_info for frontend pods (9bde9c23-16c2-4fbe-a2bb-d17452ba9cd8-t1:a280bbd7-53e9-4048-921c-46429ebc1d2d), the >0 restart query and the ready-vs-available deployment comparison (771c18b3-b2ba-4d73-aa2b-2bc114ab4da5-t0:48129aa9-4579-4454-8c5b-4b287b76b198 and 771c18b3-b2ba-4d73-aa2b-2bc114ab4da5-t1:3f1fd604-dfa8-476f-accd-22fee047a395), and a frontend error-log filter (27cd5aaa-4826-4509-8a5c-8dc859d37bd9-t0:c00fc55f-4a57-49e7-9469-2e645bd0091b); metrics named for HTTP/gRPC error rates of these services are not present in this Prometheus at all.

The Loki query for namespace hotel-reservation was cut at its 100-line limit and returned only lines timestamped 2026-11-23T22:20:36.819Z-22:20:39.330Z (view b9d51596-6e20-4e55-9714-301436693ae8-t0:f18964ff-5183-4f3a-aa19-1d20acdc85ce, incomplete true), so application log history earlier in the window was not read.

The frontend Deployment received a second, no-op rollout at 22:20:37Z with an unchanged pod template (same image digest and env as frontend-68745cb99c) and the trigger of that rollout is unknown; change history is not integrated in this Run, so it cannot be attributed. It is not impact evidence: the new frontend pod served /hotels with 200 status.

The NetworkPolicy effect is inferred from the policy object plus client-side immediate failures; no CNI/kubelet packet-drop logs or network error counters were available, and the recommendation pod logged nothing after the policy was created, so drops were not observed directly.

The declared qps/retry settings I read - RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=500 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 on Deployment rate, RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=100, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0 and RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2 on Deployment search - were not exercised, since their counters were zero at 22:20:48Z, so their behaviour under load is unchecked.
next_steps: Ask the owner of NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation (managedFields manager OpenAPI-Generator, last update 2026-11-23T22:20:36Z) to confirm whether the deny-all segmentation was intended, and add the intended allow rules or remove it.

After any change, verify recovery by checking that frontend HTTP GET /recommendations returns 200, that recommendation appears in Jaeger with server spans for /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations, and that recommendation can reach mongodb-recommendation:27017.
Separately establish why Deployment frontend rolled to generation 2 at 22:20:37Z with an unchanged pod template, since the change-history integration is unavailable in this Run.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
